findings.title: Zero-only fallback does not protect approximate t CI against severe finite-sample undercoverage
findings.why: The Neyman variance estimator is conservative in expectation, not a pointwise upper bound for the true randomization variance. Near-zero positive variance estimates bypass the Vhat=0 fallback. Satterthwaite with df capped at19 does not make the t pivot exact for bounded four-slot randomization outcomes.
findings.counterexample: For19 tasks, all4 slots have Y(R)=Y(B)=.5. For task20, both arms have identical slot outcomes[0,.001,.999,1]. All unit treatment effects and the finite80-slot mean effect are exactly0. Of6 equally probable task20 assignments,2 produce Delta_hat=+/−.04995 and Vhat=1.25e−9>0, df=2, halfwidth=.0001521217461. Neither triggers fallback. The other4 intervals contain0. Exact coverage is4/6=66.6667%. A positive CI-lower>.02 event occurs with probability1/6 if that CI alone authorizes MUE superiority.
findings.limitation: This falsifies the advertised95% t interval/CI-only MUE calibration; it does not demonstrate failure of the Fisher p test. The exact two-sided sharp-null p for an extreme assignment in this example is1/3.
findings.minimum_correction: Keep the t interval as a clearly approximate descriptive interval only. The simplest valid confirmatory mean/MUE rule uses the bounded-outcome interval below for every complete dataset, not only when Vhat=0. Alternatively retain only Fisher sharp-null confirmation and report average/MUE evidence as approximate and non-confirmatory. Do not repair this with an arbitrary near-zero epsilon threshold.
findings.cheap_check: The six assignments are exhaustively enumerated in numerical_check; no model or benchmark data is involved.

required_math_specifications.title: Fix potential-outcome units and define always-valid bounded mean interval
assumptions: 4 fresh slot identities and their scheduling/resource states are defined before arm assignment
each task independently selects2 of4 slots uniformly for R
potential outcome of a slot does not change with other slots arm assignments; no cross-run outputs or assignment-induced resource/cache interference
all primary U are observed and lie in[0,1]; retain existing unknown rule otherwise
required_math_specifications.finite_variance_definition: S uses denominator4−1 over the4 fixed potential outcomes; observed s uses denominator2−1 within an assigned arm.
required_math_specifications.interpretation: This is finite-sample conservative under the declared independent task allocation and no-interference assumptions. At T20 it is wide: Delta_hat must exceed about.62736 for lower>.02. That loss of precision is substantive and must not be hidden by relabeling the approximate t interval as confirmatory.

required_math_specifications.title: Specify the Monte Carlo Fisher statistic, ties, and null
required_math_specifications.draws: For each b=1,...,99999 draw independently one of the6 allocations for each of the20 tasks, with replacement across b; preserve observed outcomes under the Fisher sharp null. Fix the PRNG implementation as well as seed20260909.
required_math_specifications.ties: Use >= including ties, not >. Freeze any floating-comparison rule.
required_math_specifications.interpretation: Plus-one Monte Carlo randomization p is appropriate for this sharp null with the stated sampling rule. It is not an exhaustive6^20 p calculation and it is not an exact weak mean-null test. No separate mathematical fault was found in this revised Fisher specification.
